# xshield_azure_enforcement_status (Data Source)

Reports the policy Xshield expects for an Azure subscription and region, and what it could not enforce there, without changing anything, so it can run inside a `check` block.

A workload Xshield refuses is left out of `xshield_azure_enforcement_snapshot` and keeps the network security groups it has: the refusal is reported only here, in `notices`, so a plan that changes nothing for a workload does not by itself mean its policy is enforced.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The snapshot leaves out a workload Xshield refuses, so a plan that changes nothing for it does not mean its
# policy is enforced. These checks report each refusal, high-severity drift the cloud connector observes, and a
# pipeline that has stopped resolving the expected version.
data "xshield_azure_enforcement_status" "this" {
  cloud_account_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  region           = "eastus2"
}

locals {
  status        = data.xshield_azure_enforcement_status.this
  where         = "${local.status.cloud_account_id}/${local.status.region}"
  max_check_age = "24h"
  refused       = [for n in local.status.notices : "  ${coalesce(n.asset_name, n.asset_id)}: ${n.reason}: ${n.message}" if n.code == "assetRefused"]
  drift_high = [
    for f in local.status.drift_findings : "  ${f.kind} ${coalesce(f.resource_name, f.resource)}: ${f.detail} (fixed by: ${f.restoration})" if f.severity == "high"
  ]
  pipeline_stale = local.status.published && timecmp(timeadd(coalesce(local.status.last_checked_at, "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"), local.max_check_age), plantimestamp()) < 0
}

check "xshield_workloads_refused" {
  assert {
    condition     = length(local.refused) == 0
    error_message = join("\n", concat(["Xshield cannot enforce policy on these workloads in ${local.where}:"], local.refused))
  }
}

check "xshield_drift_high" {
  assert {
    condition     = length(local.drift_high) == 0
    error_message = join("\n", concat(["Xshield sees high-severity drift in ${local.where}:"], local.drift_high))
  }
}

check "xshield_pipeline_stale" {
  assert {
    condition     = !local.pipeline_stale
    error_message = "No enforcement plan for ${local.where} has resolved the version Xshield expects in the last ${local.max_check_age}: run the enforcement workspace."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cloud_account_id` (String) Azure subscription ID to report on.
- `region` (String) Azure region to report on, such as `eastus2`.

### Read-Only

- `applied_at` (String) When the latest receipt was recorded.
- `applied_interface_associations` (Map of String) From the last receipt: the interface association import ID, `<network interface ID>|<network security group ID>` of each resource the enforcement module created, keyed as the module keys `azurerm_network_interface_security_group_association.this`. Empty before the first receipt.
- `applied_network_security_groups` (Map of String) From the last receipt: the network security group ID of each resource the enforcement module created, keyed as the module keys `azurerm_network_security_group.this`. Empty before the first receipt.
- `applied_subnet_associations` (Map of String) From the last receipt: the subnet association import ID, the subnet's ID of each resource the enforcement module created, keyed as the module keys `azurerm_subnet_network_security_group_association.this`. Empty before the first receipt.
- `applied_version` (String) Version in the latest apply receipt. Null when nothing has been applied.
- `drift_evaluated` (Boolean) Whether drift could be evaluated: it needs an applied receipt and a cloud connector observation taken after it. An observation older than the latest apply describes resources that apply replaced, so it is not evaluated.
- `drift_findings` (List of Object) Differences between the subscription as observed and the snapshot as applied. `kind`: `groupMissing` when a network security group of Xshield's is gone, `ruleMissing` or `ruleModified` when one of its rules is gone or no longer matches, `ruleUnmanaged` when a group holds a rule named as Xshield names its rules, or any rule once the latest receipt set `exclusive_rules`, that the snapshot does not hold, `memberUnattached` when a workload's network interface or subnet no longer carries its group, and `groupUnmanaged` when a network security group carries the pipeline's tags but the applied state does not hold it. `severity`: `high` where access may be wider than approved or a workload is unenforced, otherwise `medium`. `restoration`: `pipeline` when the next enforcement apply restores it, `manual` when a person must: for `groupUnmanaged`, which Terraform cannot see and must be removed by hand, for `ruleUnmanaged` on a rule not named as Xshield's while the latest receipt did not set `exclusive_rules`, and for `groupMissing` and `memberUnattached` on a group of yours. `resource`: Azure resource ID of the affected group or rule, or the Xshield asset ID for `memberUnattached`. `resource_name`: the name of what `resource` identifies: the workload for `memberUnattached`, the group for a group finding, and the rule for a rule finding. `key`: snapshot key involved: the group's key in `xshield_azure_enforcement_snapshot`, or `<group key>/<rule name>` for a missing or changed rule. `detail`: human-readable explanation. `detected_at`: when Xshield recorded the finding, which stays recorded until an observation shows it gone; null for a state the next enforcement apply clears or makes, which Xshield does not record as drift. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--drift_findings))
- `drift_observed_at` (String) When the cloud connector's latest observation was taken.
- `expected_version` (String) Version Xshield expects to be enforced, the hash of everything it asks for.
- `last_checked_at` (String) When an enforcement plan last resolved the expected version. A stale value means the pipeline has stopped running, whatever `state` says.
- `notices` (List of Object) What Xshield could not enforce in the expected version, and why. A refused workload gets no network security group of Xshield's and keeps the groups it has, until the cause is fixed. `reason`: why, such as `NO_FREE_LEVEL` when the workload's network interfaces carry a network security group of yours and it has no subnet Xshield can use, which its message names, `INTERFACES_IN_SEVERAL_SUBNETS` when its network interfaces are in more than one subnet and one carries a group of yours, so no one subnet would cover them all, `SUBNET_IN_ANOTHER_REGION` when it is enforced on a subnet whose virtual network is in another region than the workload, as a private endpoint's subnet can be, so none of its rules is written in the snapshot of the workload's region, which its message names, `DISCOVER_FAILED:NO_SUBNET` when discovery shows neither, `NOT_EXPRESSIBLE_ON_AZURE:<detail>` when its policy holds a rule no network security rule can hold, `RULE_BUDGET` when its rules, with those of the workloads sharing its group, pass what one group holds, `ENDPOINT_NETWORK_POLICIES_OFF` when it is reached through a private endpoint whose subnet's private endpoint network policies are neither `Enabled` nor `NetworkSecurityGroupEnabled`, so a group there would not filter its traffic, `NO_PRIVATE_INBOUND` when a Function App with inbound policy has no private endpoint, `INTEGRATION_SUBNET_SHARED` when a Function App with outbound policy shares its VNet integration subnet with other apps, `DISCOVER_FAILED:NO_INTEGRATION_SUBNET_RANGE` when discovery gives no address range of that subnet, `CONNECTOR_GROUP_UNRECORDED` when the cloud connector's own group is on the workload and the connector holds no record of the group it displaced, so it cannot hand the workload over and its group goes on enforcing it, `RULE_BEYOND_WORKLOAD` when its rules would go into a group of yours and one names a service tag where it names the workload, so it cannot be held to the workload's own addresses, or `NO_FREE_PRIORITY` when the first rule of the group of yours its rules would go into leaves too few priorities below it, in a direction, for Xshield's rules there, which its message names: move your rules up, and Xshield writes the workload's rules once the cloud connector observes the group. An `observationStale` notice is about the subscription and region: the cloud connector has not observed them for three observation intervals since the last apply or observation, so a change made in Azure since is not shown as drift. An `associationHeld` notice names a group of Xshield's that this version no longer places, whose network interface or subnet the cloud connector has shown carrying a network security group of yours since the last apply. Azure removes an association by clearing its level's group, so removing Xshield's would remove yours: the `azure` enforcement module keeps it in its state, unchanged, until the level carries no group of yours. An `assetContained` notice, with reason `BREACH_ACTIVE`, names a workload the cloud connector contains under a breach response: its group is on the workload's network interface or subnet in place of Xshield's, and the module keeps Xshield's association as it is until the containment is reverted. An `associationKept` notice names a workload that this version places at another network interface or subnet: Xshield keeps the association it leaves, with that group and its rules, until a receipt shows the new placement applied, so a workload moving between its network interface and its subnet keeps its old group for one more apply. A `levelSharedWithContained` notice names a workload whose subnet a contained workload shares, so the connector's group covers it too and it is not synchronized until the containment is reverted. A `customerGroupWritten` notice names a workload whose rules Xshield writes into the group of yours on the network interface its enforcement scope names, or on its subnet, which `group` names. A `levelFallback` notice names a workload whose enforcement scope is its network interface but whose interface cannot take a group, such as a private endpoint's or a scale set instance's, so its rules go on its subnet, and `reason` says why. A `customerGroupRulesRemoved` notice names a group of yours, by `group`, that a write of the group as a whole, such as an apply of a configuration declaring its rules inline, took Xshield's rules out of at `since`, naming who made it; the enforcement apply puts them back, and the notice stays until a later write of the group keeps them all, which declaring its rules through `xshield_azure_security_rules` does. A `customerGroupCarriedByYourCode` notice names a group of yours whose latest such write, at `since`, kept every rule of Xshield's there, and `customerGroupCarryBehind` one whose latest write kept an earlier version's rules: that configuration carries the new ones at its next apply. Either way the enforcement apply goes on writing the rules. A `connectorHandsOver` notice names a workload the cloud connector enforced with a group of its own, which `group` names: once this version is applied, the connector puts Xshield's group in place of its group in one change. Where its group displaced one of yours, Xshield writes the workload's rules into your group first, and the connector puts your group back only once an observation shows it holding every one of them; until then the connector's group goes on enforcing the workload, which is no drift. Its group then stays in the subscription, detached, for you to delete, unless the connector's role lets it delete the group itself. A `testAllowsCarried` notice names a workload whose Test mode allows Xshield keeps in the group of yours that `group` names, as its subnet already let that traffic through one; a group of yours otherwise gets no Test mode allow, which would let through traffic your rules deny. They go once the workload leaves Test mode. `code`: `assetRefused`, `assetContained`, `levelSharedWithContained`, `customerGroupWritten`, `levelFallback`, `customerGroupRulesRemoved`, `customerGroupCarriedByYourCode`, `customerGroupCarryBehind`, `testAllowsCarried`, `connectorHandsOver`, `associationHeld`, `associationKept` or `observationStale`. `asset_id`: the Xshield asset the notice is about, when there is one. `asset_name`: the workload as Azure names it, when Xshield knows it. `group`: for `associationHeld` and `associationKept`, the group by its key in the snapshot; for `customerGroupWritten`, `testAllowsCarried` and the three about writes of your group, the name of your group; for `connectorHandsOver`, the name of the cloud connector's group; null for `assetRefused`, `assetContained`, `levelSharedWithContained`, `levelFallback` and `observationStale`. `since`: for `observationStale`, the last apply or observation it counts from; for the three about writes of your group, the write; null for every other code. `message`: what happened and what to do about it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--notices))
- `pending_since` (String) When the oldest policy change not yet applied was published.
- `published` (Boolean) False while Xshield has published nothing for this subscription and region. `state` is then `unpublished`, `expected_version` is null and `notices` is empty, so checks stay quiet.
- `state` (String) `converged` when the latest receipt is for the expected version, `pending` when Xshield expects newer policy than was applied, `unapplied` when nothing has been applied yet, `unpublished` when Xshield has published nothing to apply, and `handedOver` when the subscription moved to connector delivery.
